context: a letter from J. D. Hooker, which you are answering
exchanges:
Your photograph tells me where Herbert got his Moses for the Fresco in the House of Lords.—horns & halo & all— Well done William. Your mouth comes out funnily like F. Wedgwoods! Do pray send me one for Thwaites, who will be enchanted with it. Oliver is calling out too for one.

The best news in your letter is, that I may run down with a possibility of seeing you. I shall do so as soon as I possibly can—but am engaged both 2 Sundays, to come. I shall be repaid with seeing Mrs Darwin if you are not well enough:—& more than repaid—so you need not mind being ill!!!

I can get our agent to look out for a good ship for Scott for Calcutta direct, if he will let me know about time of starting.

I am delighted to hear of the Oxlip case.— it explains why the oxlip varies so much—now towards C. now towards P.—as I observed it to do about Hitcham— it does not however quite explain to me why in certain large patches it is so uniform as to variety as it certainly is.— Except indeed you suppose that insects may take pollen from C to P. or vice versa only.

I will ask Harvey about the Dandelion— I send you another case of his which I must also see to. (NB. I do not hold that sports of branches &c do not revert)—

I will write next week about the plants.

No more at present | Yr affec | J D Hooker

Many thanks for yr photograph which we were both glad to get. It is an excellent one & to my mind gives your character better than any one I have seen. I enclose 2 more of mine for Oliver & Thwaites. Funnily enough the boys declared it was like Moses. I return Harveys letter as I suppose you mean to keep it otherwise I would. Stir him up to publish on this & Dandelion—; Ovules of latter differ.

If I can lay my hands on a specimen I will enclose a head. With respect to Oxlip I strongly suspect that the uniform P. elatior is really a distinct species but I will try next spring & perhaps publish a little paper on the subject.

Many thanks for offer about ship for Scott. He has just sent a curious paper on sterility of Passiflora; it will ultimately prove that nothing is so variable as the reproductive function. You told me Decaisne said that Delphinium is not crossed.— I have now found that the flowers of D. consolida artificially fertilised under a net produce twice as many seed as the untouched flowers under the same net.

You are a real good man to talk of coming here soon

yours affectionately | C Darwin

I doubt whether I shall get a young Vanilla from Veitch: if you can lend or give me a growing one it will be a priceless treasure

Can the Dandelion case have any relation to the difference of achenia in certain genera in ray & central florets?
